title: One model spelling, or a translation with a test that boots a container
description:
Found by mrn's worker while building the work-type table (finding 52f48872 on epic/wne), and verified 2026-09-22.

Two spellings of the same model are in the tree:

  image/common.sh:256 accepts workers-ai/* and line 269 DIES on anything else:
    'cannot tell which provider serves the model ... qualify it with one of
     workers-ai/..., anthropic/..., openai/... or openrouter/...'
  wrangler.toml's RUN_WORKER_MODEL examples use that same workers-ai/... prefix.

  Everything else in this repository - profiles-herdr/, .tick/runners.toml's
  [roles.implement], and the work-type table mrn just committed - spells it
  cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3, which is the pi profile spelling.

So a work-type table value routed into a container boot is refused at startup on a
message about providers, having nothing to do with the tick that was dispatched.

This belongs to xte because xte is where a model name first travels from ticfac's
config INTO a container. njj pairs pi with the routing and is the tick that would
otherwise ship the mismatch.

Settle it one of two ways, and say which in the tick's report:
  - ONE spelling per consumer, with the translation at the boundary that crosses
    between them, or
  - one spelling everywhere, migrating whichever side is wrong.

THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST, and is why the finding says 'nothing in this tick's Go
tests can catch it': no Go test boots a container, so the two spellings can disagree
indefinitely without any gate going red. Whatever the resolution, it needs a test that
exercises the actual boundary - common.sh's model parse against the value ticfac would
really hand it - rather than two sides each asserting their own spelling is fine.
acceptance_criteria: A model name that ticfac's config can produce is accepted by image/common.sh's provider parse, proven by a test that runs the real parse against the real configured value rather than a fixture of either spelling; and the repository has one documented answer for which spelling each consumer uses
